name: Piecemeal Food Provisions
desc:
Website: https://www.piecemealfood.biz/

Instagram: @piecemeal_food

Facebook: PieceMeal Food Provisions

In 2020, PieceMeal emerged from Kara Friesen's unwavering passion for promoting convenient options for local eating. Driven by a deep-rooted love for her community and a commitment to sustainability, Kara set out to create a culinary venture that would not only taste delicious but support local farmers and producers.

Understanding that food should be a delightful experience, culinary artisan Fiona Lewis crafts delicious recipes, spice blends, and sauces that perfectly complement the bounty of locally sourced produce here in the Annapolis Valley. Each dish is thoughtfully curated, emphasizing the natural flavours of the ingredients while celebrating the richness of local offerings.

By forging strong partnerships with local farmers and producers, PieceMeal ensures that their creations are not only bursting with taste but also contribute to the thriving ecosystem of sustainable agriculture.

Beyond the dishes they prepare, PieceMeal is on a mission to inspire conscious eating habits within communities. Kara believes that the choices we make in our daily meals have a profound impact on our health, environment, and the well-being of local producers. Through their approachable and flavorful offerings, PieceMeal endeavours to show that supporting local eating can be both enjoyable and meaningful.

How you can support Piecemeal Food: Subscribe to a meal kit through the WFM2Go, sign up for their newsletter, or check out the educational resources found on their website.

name: Olde Furrow Farm
desc:
Website: https://www.oldefurrowfarm.com/

Instagram: @oldefurrow

Facebook: Olde Furrow Farm

Meet Courtney and Adam Webster, the husband and wife duo who are the proud owners of Olde Furrow Farm. Their passion for growing things and immersing themselves in the farming lifestyle has led them on a fulfilling journey. Today, they carry on a cherished tradition of farming that spans three generations, cultivating their land in the picturesque Annapolis Valley.

At Olde Furrow Farm, the Websters adhere to a set of core principles that guide their approach to farming. They prioritize the use of non-GMO seeds and completely avoid the use of harmful chemicals, embracing a more sustainable and eco-friendly path. Understanding the significance of a balanced ecosystem, they apply companion planting techniques and crop rotation, which fosters healthier soil and enhances overall biodiversity.

Recognizing the value of beneficial insects, they create a welcoming environment that attracts these helpers, promoting natural pest control without resorting to harmful pesticides. Additionally, they harness the power of compost teas and nutrient-rich compost, enriching their soil and providing their plants with the nourishment they need to flourish.

Olde Furrow Farm is a labour of love and dedication to responsible, regenerative agriculture. Courtney and Adam's commitment to these principles not only yields high-quality produce but also contributes to the preservation and enhancement of the beautiful Annapolis Valley's natural environment. With each harvest, they celebrate their connection to the land and the joy of nurturing it for future generations to come.

How you can support Olde Furrow Farm: Sign up for their CSA, visit their open house, A Place of Fruition, every Thursday from 2pm-6pm, or purchase their produce and seeds through the WFM2GO.

name: Lorax Woodlands
desc:
Lorax Woodlands is a charming intentional community nestled in the rolling hills near Black River in Kings County, Nova Scotia, just a short ten-minute drive from Wolfville. The community's foundation rests upon a historic 200-acre farm dating back to the mid-1700s, which Lorax Woodlands acquired in 1999. Utilizing approximately 30 acres of cleared land, they divided it into eight lots, while the remaining 170 acres of woodland became collectively owned land, reserved for recreation, forest conservation, and education.

This woodland is an integral part of the Acadian forest, boasting a diverse array of hardwood and softwood species and teeming with abundant wildlife. Its enchanting features include beaver ponds, a marsh, and two streams that gracefully flow into Lumsden Lake. Lorax Woodlands has a resolute commitment to preserving this communal woodland, adopting sustainable forest management practices and ecologically sound land-use strategies to encourage the land's indigenous biodiversity and natural resources over time. Their vision is to set an example for others as a model community.

The name "Lorax Woodlands" draws inspiration from Dr. Seuss' tale, "The Lorax," which portrays a place ravaged by greedy deforestation. The character of the Lorax represents the voice of wisdom, determined to safeguard the creatures and the forest. For the community, this name symbolizes their aspiration to cherish their surroundings, harmoniously coexist with nature and their neighbours, and, in their small way, contribute to a more sustainable way of living. Throughout their journey, Lorax Woodlands takes pride in what they have achieved over the past two decades, and they strive to leave a positive impact on the environment, honouring the spirit of The Lorax.

name: Revival Seeds
desc:
Website: https://revivalseeds.ca/

Instagram: @revivalseeds

Facebook: Revival Seeds

Youtube: Revival Seeds

Nestled in Middleton, you'll find Revival Seeds, a thriving farm and business. This family-owned and operated venture is led by Ken and Kathy, joined by their dedicated daughter, Mallory Byrka. Their unwavering commitment is to offer customers hardy heirloom, open-pollinated, and diverse seed varieties cultivated under strict organic production principles.

Revival Seeds honours a century-old tradition that began nearly 100 years ago on the prairie soils near Riding Mountain, Manitoba. Continuing the legacy of the original family farm, the Byrka family carries forward the passion for seeds and gardening passed down through generations.

With their roots deeply connected to the land and their hearts dedicated to preserving heirloom seeds, Revival Seeds strives to provide customers with premium-quality seeds that embody the richness of heritage varieties. Their organic cultivation methods and dedication to sustainable practices ensure that every seed is nurtured with care and reverence.

At Revival Seeds, the love for the land, the legacy of family farming, and the pursuit of preserving genetic diversity converge, making it a cherished destination for those seeking authentic, time-tested seeds and a true connection to the earth.

How you can support Revival Seeds: Visit their website and browse through their large collection of seeds, or sign up for their mailing list.

name: As The River Bends Retreat
desc:
Website: https://www.astheriverbendsretreat.com/

Instagram: @as_the_river_bends_retreat

Facebook: As The River Bends Retreat

The River Bends Retreat is a harmonious eco-conscious haven, nestled beside the serene Halfway River. This tranquil sanctuary provides nature-inspired experiences through the property that change with the seasons and reflect the offerings of the natural world. Embracing a host of eco-friendly elements, their one-of-a-kind domes offer guests a chance to immerse themselves in the beauty of nature. Drift off to sleep under a blanket of stars and awaken to the soothing melodies of birdsong. At the retreat, guests can truly disconnect from the outside world to reconnect with themselves and the wonders of the natural environment.

How you can support As The River Bends Retreat: Book an evening stay at one of their many beautiful domes (https://www.astheriverbendsretreat.com/domes) or sign up to their email list to be the first to know about their community events.

name: Seven Acres Farm & Ferments
desc:
Website: https://www.sevenacresfarm.ca/

Instagram: @sevenacresfarmandferments

Facebook: Seven Acres Farm and Ferments

Seven Acres Farm specializes in crafting a seasonally-influenced line of hand-crafted, small-batch, fermented sauerkrauts, kimchis, and pickles. Their dedication to ecological regeneration plays a significant role in their farming approach. Mindful of their land management practices, they prioritize the well-being of the creatures, soil, and water that share the space with them. Embracing techniques such as no-spray crop management, cover crops, and crop rotation, they work to ensure sustainable and responsible farming.

To foster a thriving ecosystem, Seven Acres Farm goes beyond traditional farming methods. They leave parts of their farm and forest undisturbed, and thoughtfully plant hedgerows and perennials that offer essential support to animals, birds, and insects throughout all seasons.

Passionate about sourcing top-quality ingredients, the farm proudly collaborates with local Nova Scotia farmers who share their commitment to ecologically sensitive growing practices. By integrating their values into every aspect of their work, Seven Acres Farm strives to make a positive impact on the environment while providing their customers with exceptional and sustainable products.

How to support Seven Acres Farms: Apart from making their ferments available at a roadside farm stand (open daily from 7am-8pm) and their products can be found on the shelves of several esteemed retailers across Nova Scotia, you can visit Jocelyn and Tim at their booth during the Saturday Wolfville Farmers' Market.

name: Soft Pine Wellness
desc:
Website: https://www.softpinewellness.ca/

Instagram: @soft.pine.forest.wellness

Soft Pine Wellness, established in 2021 by Wil Brunner, aims to empower individuals in discovering, exploring, and deepening their personal connections with nature. Through forest bathing walks and experiences guided by Wil, participants embark on a journey of sensory activities that attune their bodies, minds, and hearts to the natural world.

For those seeking a more intimate experience, Soft Pine Wellness offers the option of booking private sessions for individuals and groups. These sessions can take place in a location of the participant's choice or at a local setting where public walks are also conducted. Wil can tailor specific elements and the overall flow to suit the unique preferences and goals of the participants.

Recognizing the diverse needs of people and groups, Soft Pine Wellness ensures that their nature therapy, forest bathing, and related experiences are trauma-informed and rooted in extensively researched concepts. It is widely acknowledged that spending time in nature can significantly enhance mental and physical well-being, foster personal growth, and cultivate joy and contentment.

Beyond promoting human health, these experiences also instill a sense of stewardship and conservation for the precious land and waters on which we all rely. Soft Pine Wellness stands committed to nurturing a deeper connection between individuals and the natural world, fostering a profound appreciation for its beauty and resources.

How you can support Soft Pine Wellness: Participate in a community forest bathing walk, book a private experience, or check out one of the many resources available here.

name: Wholesum Refillery
desc:
Website: https://www.wholesumrefillery.com/

Instagram: @wholesumrefillery

Facebook: Wholesum Refillery

Wholesum Refillery is the shared vision of Rachael and Krista, childhood friends driven by a desire to make a meaningful impact. Their passion lies in reducing single-use plastic consumption within their community, recognizing that positive change often begins with small steps in local neighborhoods. Their mission is to establish a welcoming space where individuals can take pride in the products they purchase and transition to low-waste shopping practices.

At Wholesum Refillery, an array of home, bath, and beauty products are offered in bulk, ranging from shampoo to household cleaners. Emphasizing sustainability, customers are encouraged to bring their clean, previously used containers to be refilled!

How you can support Wholesum Refillery: Stop by their storefront in Kentville to shop local or sign up for their email list!

name: Herbal Hill Farm
desc:
Instagram: @herbalhillfarm

Facebook: Herbal Hill Farm

Michelle Wolf of Herbal Hill Farm has been an organic gardener and herbalist for over 25 years. Together with her husband Al, they run a farmers’ market business, cultivating perennial plants, seeds, veggies, herbs, berries, flowers, and ornamental plants on their family's homestead. They also enjoy wild-crafting, gathering natural treasures from the wild for their signature products. Their gardening philosophy revolves around ecological principles, emphasizing biodiversity, hand tools, simplicity, and beauty.

Read more about Michelle’s journey here.

name: Gaspereau Valley Fibres
desc:
Website: https://www.gaspereauvalleyfibres.ca/

Instagram: @gaspereauvalleyfibres

Facebook: Gaspereau Valley Fibres

Gaspereau Valley Fibres is a family-owned farm and wool shop situated in the Gaspereau Valley, located just outside of Wolfville. They specialize in providing natural, locally grown fibre yarns. Their inventory caters to knitters, spinners, weavers, and felters, encompassing spinning wheels, looms, tools, and notions to meet the needs of crafters at all skill levels.

With a remarkable experience of over 25 years, Gaspereau Valley Fibres has dedicated its efforts to raising and caring for Cotswold sheep, nurturing a flock of over 60 of these splendid animals. Their commitment extends to processing approximately 200 kgs of fleece, which is thoughtfully sold in their farm wool shop.

Beyond providing exceptional products, Gaspereau Valley Fibres fosters a sense of community by hosting an array of classes, where individuals can enhance their skills and connect with fellow fibre enthusiasts. Their approach to wool and farming practices demonstrates how businesses and individuals can contribute to climate action by making conscious choices that prioritize sustainability, local sourcing, and environmental stewardship.

How you can support Gaspereau Valley Fibres: Visit the farm and wool shop, register for a beginner class, or sign up for their newsletter.

name: Front Street Community Oven
desc:
Website: https://frontstreetoven.ca/

Instagram: @frontstreetoven

Facebook: Front Street Community Oven in Wolfville

The Front Street Community Oven is a popular and unique community gathering space located in the heart of Wolfville. The wood-fired outdoor oven serves as a focal point for various community events and activities. Throughout the year, the Front Street Community Oven hosts numerous events and workshops, including pizza nights, bread-baking sessions, and educational programs focused on traditional baking methods and sustainable living practices. By embracing the values of local sourcing, waste reduction, and energy efficiency, the community oven contributes to greatly climate action efforts and has become a cherished spot for gatherings, celebrations, and fostering a strong sense of community in Wolfville.



How you can support “the oven”: Drop in to the Community Cookout from 6pm-8pm on Thursdays, volunteer to be a Firemaster, become an Oven Patron, or sign up for their email list.

name: Valley Waste Resource Management
desc:
Website: https://www.vwrm.com/

Instagram: @valleywaste

Facebook: Valley Waste-Resource Management

Valley Waste is part of a network of seven solid waste regions in Nova Scotia, all working collaboratively to advance waste diversion and prevention efforts on a regional scale. This approach allows for greater efficiencies and financial viability when it comes to recycling and composting initiatives.

With a strong commitment to waste reduction and diversion, Valley Waste provides a range of valuable resources to support residents, students, and businesses in their sustainability endeavors. These resources include classroom presentations, informative educational videos, residential education programs, eye-opening site tours, outreach initiatives for businesses and communities, community clean-up events, and seasonal property education.

By offering these comprehensive services, Valley Waste aims to empower individuals and organizations to play an active role in reducing waste and embracing more sustainable practices. Through education and community engagement, they strive to make a positive impact on waste management, environmental conservation, and the overall well-being of the region.

Did you know? Valley Waste’s administration building was one of the first commercial buildings in Canada to be accredited for both LEED Gold and Passive House certifications!

name: EOS Natural Foods
desc:
Website: https://www.eosnaturalfoods.ca/

Instagram: @eosnaturalfoods

Facebook: Eos Natural Foods

For over 50 years, Eos Natural Foods has been a staple of wellness in Wolfville. Established in 1973 as a co-op, Eos provided a welcoming space for locals to connect while filling their pantries with nourishing foods. Embracing a commitment to supporting the community, they prioritize sourcing from local businesses whenever feasible, promoting sustainability and fostering a sense of togetherness among neighbours.

Eos is devoted to offering ethically derived products, even if they cannot be found locally, ensuring their customers have access to a diverse range of wholesome options. To reduce waste and promote eco-friendliness, many of their products are available in bulk, encouraging a more sustainable approach to shopping.

Eos is dedicated to making wellness accessible to all, as evidenced by its daily discount for students and seniors. By fostering an inclusive environment and providing quality products, this small but mighty shop continues to be a driving force in promoting health and well-being within the Wolfville community.

name: Acadia Community Fridge
desc:
Instagram: @acadia_community_fridge

The Acadia Community Fridge serves as a hub that brings students together to enjoy meals, foster connections, acquire new skills, and combat food waste. This space allows the individuals within the community to come together and share food from various sources, including surplus from supermarkets, local food businesses, producers, households, and gardens. It's a place where everyone can contribute and benefit, promoting a sense of solidarity and sustainability in the community.

Community fridges help reduce food waste by providing a space for individuals and businesses to share surplus food that might otherwise be tossed. This is crucial to climate action because when food is wasted, all the resources used in its production, such as water, energy, and land, are also wasted. Community fridges provide an opportunity to engage with the student population and promote discussions about sustainable food systems, climate change, and the importance of reducing waste.

name: Acadia Community Farm
desc:
Website: https://farm.acadiau.ca/home.html

Instagram: @acadiacommunityfarm

Facebook: The Acadia Community Farm

The Acadia Community Farm has been an integral piece of Wolfville since it began in 2008 thanks to the overwhelming support from students and volunteers who actively manage and maintain the farm. Every season, organic produce is grown and harvested for the Acadia dining hall as well as donated to the local food bank.

As part of its educational mission, the Acadia Farm hosts seasonal workshops facilitated by local experts, covering various topics such as permaculture, organic gardening, and seed saving. These workshops provide valuable knowledge and skill-building opportunities for participants.

The farm also serves as a practical teaching resource and field research site for various Acadia courses. It plays a significant role in community development, biology, environmental studies, sustainability studies, and other disciplines, providing students with hands-on experience and real-world applications of their learning.

name: Flying Squirrel Adventures
desc:
Website: https://valleyflyingsquirrel.wordpress.com/

Instagram: @flyingsquirreladventures

Flying Squirrel Adventures is dedicated to organizing and leading captivating nature excursions, activities, and event series suitable for people of all age groups in the picturesque Annapolis Valley. Their mission is to foster a profound connection between individuals and the natural world, as well as to build a vibrant community of nature enthusiasts. The symbol of the Flying Squirrel embodies the essence of curiosity and enjoyment found in exploring the wonders of nature!

How you can support FSA:

Subscribe to their newsletter, register for a course, become a volunteer, or donate to their bursary!

name: Ann and William Truemen
desc: Ann and William Truemen, who have owned their property since 1992, made a significant commitment to climate action by refraining from logging on their land since 1997. Over the years, their opposition to logging has grown, and they now recognize the greater value of preserving their bountiful backyard over the short-lived financial gains often associated with selling portions of their lot. Their decision to refrain from logging their property and prioritize its preservation over short-term financial gains is crucial to climate action. It embodies principles of carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, sustainability, local climate regulation, and the potential to inspire others to make environmentally responsible choices.
